Hi Jules / Ana —

Attached is version 1.2 of the mutual action plan (tab: FinOps QC). Key sections I want us to sanity-check before we lock timelines: tokens-per-user assumption, expected cache hit rates, and batching strategy during peak windows. Quick highlights: 

- Baseline tokens per request: 420 tokens (prompt + expected completion)
- Projected monthly active requests: 1.2M
- Expected KV cache hit rate in first 90 days: 22% (we model conservative warm caches)
- Batching policy recommended: 50ms max wait, dynamic batch up to 32 requests (saves ~18% token CPU cost in our simulation)

Attachments: BRW_MAP_v1.2.xlsx (MAP with checkpoints), brightwell_cost_model_qc.csv (cost sensitivity).

Ask: can you confirm your realistic peak QPS and the percent of requests that include long context (>2k tokens)? Those numbers materially change the tokens/$ we surface to procurement.

Proposed next steps: 
- You review FinOps tab and reply with QPS + % long-context by EOD next Tue (7/16)
- We run a short sensitivity pass and send an updated cost sheet by 7/17
- Goal: final MAP sign-off by 7/24 so procurement can start paperwork

Thanks —

Thanks for the numbers, Jules — those burst characteristics are helpful. A few internal clarifications and an updated assumption set (see attached CSV):

- We modeled burst behavior using a peak concurrency of 380 for short bursts; the runtime uses dynamic batching plus a 50ms aggregator window by default.
- Cache hit rate: original 22% was conservative; with your expected user repeat rate and session design I bumped the working case to 34% (warm cache scenario) and left 14% for cold-starts in the sensitivity columns.
- Long-context handling: for the 8% of long-context requests we assumed model variant L-2 (higher token consumption) and a fallback policy to a quantized L-1 for non-critical generations — this reduces token compute cost by ~28% at the expense of a small quality delta we track in evals.

Attached: brightwell_cost_model_qc.csv (updated with warm/cold split and 95th percentile column per procurement ask).

Neha

Couple of tactical notes from the runtime side: 

- If Brightwell is sensitive to the 95th percentile cost, we can pre-warm cache lanes during scheduled campaign windows (automated keep-alive probes) — that raises hit-rate to ~48% in our experiments and lowers 95th percentile cost by ~12%. We should add a line item for probe costs to the MAP (small fixed $$).
- For bursts that reach ~350 QPS we recommend enabling graceful model-fallback routing: when GPU queue depth exceeds threshold, route to the quantized L-1 variant for non-blocking completions. We already captured this in the fallback_model_matrix.pdf attached.
- Batching: reduce aggregator window to 25ms only during off-peak windows where latency SLO is looser; maintain 50ms during peak to avoid harmful latency tail.

If procurement needs a one-line description of these mitigations for the SOW, I can draft language.

—Karthik

Thanks everyone — summarizing the agreed adjustments and proposed timeline below so procurement has clear artifacts to act on: 

Summary of agreed assumptions (to be reflected in final MAP):
- Working tokens/request: 420 (baseline) with long-context bucket 8% @ model L-2
- Warm cache case: 34% hit-rate; accelerated warm probes during campaign windows can lift to ~48% (small fixed probe cost added)
- Batching: 50ms aggregator window during peak; 25ms off-peak option for latency-tolerant paths
- Fallback: quantized L-1 variant for >queue-depth thresholds (reduces compute cost ~28%)
- 95th percentile column included in attached cost CSV for procurement review

Timeline / MAP milestones: 
- 7/17: Redwood sends updated cost workbook (done — attached)
- 7/19: Brightwell internal FinOps + Procurement alignment (Jules/Ana)
